meetings.title: Weekly leadership sync
segments: Morning. Helen's on her way, she's just finishing a call with the auditors. Let's start without her.
Morning.
Morning.
Morning everyone. Let's go around quickly. Aisha, pipeline first?
Q4 pipeline is about one point two million.
The two biggest deals, Globex and Arcadia, together around four hundred and twenty thousand, are both blocked on SAML SSO.
Without SSO, I'd call both of them unlikely this quarter.
How confident are you in the rest of the pipeline, the part that isn't blocked?
Reasonably. About five hundred thousand is mid-market, with normal risk.
Kestrel Logistics is the one I'm most excited about.
And Juniper is small but moving.
The rest is early stage and I wouldn't count on it this quarter.
Sorry I'm late. Aisha, what's the weighted number?
Weighted, about six hundred thousand.
With SSO committed, I'd move Globex up, and that pushes us closer to eight.
That's a third of the pipeline behind one feature.
It is. We're doing a cross-functional alignment meeting next week to make the SSO versus Jira call, because we can't staff both.
I'll come out of it with a decision and a date.
Good. I'd like that decision in writing to this group the same day.
And the board meeting is in two weeks.
I'd like the SSO decision and the Insights plan in the deck, even if it's a single slide.
That works. The alignment meeting is before then, so I'll have both.
One slide on the SSO decision and timeline, one on the Insights beta.
On retention. Net revenue retention is ninety-seven percent for the quarter, down from a hundred and two.
I'm finishing an analysis of forty-one churn and downgrade conversations.
The early read is that the top reason is 'nobody reads the feedback', not missing features.
Which accounts are driving the drop?
Mostly downgrades rather than full churn.
Harbor and Pine went from Business to Pro.
Two smaller accounts churned outright, both mentioned Jira.
And Brightline is the biggest risk ahead of us, their renewal is in about three months.
What does Brightline need to stay?
Honestly, a reason to believe the tagging will get better.
Maya and I have a call with them this week.
What was the plan number for NRR this quarter?
A hundred and three. So we're six points behind.
Some of that will come back when Harbor and Pine's usage recovers, but not all of it.
Six points is significant. Let's review it again at the end of the month.
Ninety-seven is below plan. What's the plan to get it back?
Short term, a save play for the at-risk accounts, starting with Brightline.
Longer term, honestly, Insights 2.0 is the fix, because it attacks the top churn reason directly.
What does the save play involve? Is it discounting?
No discounts unless there's no other option.
It's attention. A senior person on every at-risk account, a clear plan for what we'll fix, and early access to Insights where it makes sense.
Discounting tends to just delay the churn.
Agreed. Fix the product problem, not the price.
Good. Then I won't budget for save discounts this quarter.
On engineering. The outage follow-ups are mostly done, the lag alert shipped.
The bigger issue is on-call load.
With five engineers, it's heavy, and we're asking a lot of the team.
How close are we to the team burning out?
I want an honest answer.
Not there yet, but I can see it from here.
Pages have tripled since the outage, some of that is new alerts being noisy.
If nothing changes in the next month, I'd expect someone to start looking elsewhere.
Okay. That's clear. Thank you for saying it plainly.
Is there anything we can do for the team in the short term? Even something small.
Let's give the platform team a recovery day after the next release.
And Raj, if there's a tool or a contractor that would take pressure off on-call, bring it to Helen directly.
I'd also approve budget for an alerting tool trial, if Raj finds one that reduces noise.
That's much cheaper than burnout.
I'll look at options this week.
Thank you. That will mean a lot to them.
Related ask, Chris. Can we accelerate the staff data engineer role?
It helps on-call and it helps the clustering work.
How long does it usually take us to hire a staff engineer?
About three months from opening the role to someone starting, based on the last two.
The market's a bit better now, so maybe faster.
We have one strong candidate from a referral already, who could move quickly.
Three months is a long time to carry the on-call load.
It is, which is why the tuning work on alerts matters in the meantime.
We can cut the noise while we hire.
Helen, can we afford to open that this month instead of next quarter?
Yes, if we're comfortable pushing the second marketing hire back a quarter. That's the trade-off.
Maya, how do you feel about pushing the marketing hire? That affects Elena.
It's the right trade. Elena's stretched, but we're bringing in a contractor for the event work, which covers the most urgent gap.
The staff data engineer helps two problems at once, on-call and the model.
Let's do it. Open the staff data engineer role now, push the marketing hire.
Related, on hiring. We made an offer to Andre for the CSM role.
He accepted yesterday, starts in three weeks.
Great news.
He'll take about thirty mid-market accounts, which frees me up to spend more time on the at-risk ones. Brightline especially.
One more thing from me.
Before anyone announces pricing for the AI features, I need a cost model.
What does the AI actually cost us per customer, and what happens to margin as they grow.
Is there a rough timeline on pricing?
Prospects are starting to ask.
Once Maya has the cost numbers, I'd need about a week to model it.
So maybe two to three weeks for a proposal.
Until then, please don't quote anything for the AI features.
Understood. I'll tell people pricing comes with general availability.
Maya, is there a risk that pricing slows down the beta?
No. The beta is free for design partners, so pricing doesn't block it.
It only matters for general availability, and that's gated on model accuracy anyway, which will take longer than the pricing work.
Good. Then there's no reason to rush pricing. Get it right.
Music to my ears.
Understood. I'll get cost numbers from Priya, and you and I can work on pricing together before it goes anywhere.
Anything else? Okay. One thing from me, then.
I want us to be careful about how we talk about AI externally.
Everyone is saying AI. We should only say it when we can show it.
Agreed. The beta is private for exactly that reason.
We'll show it to customers who can see it working on their own data before we say anything publicly.
Good. Same time next week.
Good. Thanks all. Short and useful.
